edges.effect_quant: Large-scale conditional cash transfer analyses in Brazil link high coverage to lower mortality, including an overall age-standardized mortality rate ratio of 0.824 (95% CI 0.807-0.842) and under-5 mortality rate ratio of 0.67 (95% CI 0.65-0.69), while municipal analyses also suggest lower diarrhea mortality in young children when cash-transfer coverage is combined with strong environmental services.
edges.population: low-income populations exposed to conditional or broad public cash-transfer programs
edges.mechanism: Cash transfers can reduce mortality by improving food security, treatment seeking, transport to care, and the ability of households to absorb health shocks. The mortality effect is usually strongest when transfers reach the poorest households at scale and are paired with functioning health, water, sanitation, and social-protection systems.
edges.summary: The overall evidence points toward a real mortality benefit at population scale, particularly for child survival and other poverty-sensitive outcomes. The best modern evidence comes from large Brazilian longitudinal analyses, while older reviews support a broader child-health pathway through improved nutrition, service use, and reduced morbidity.
edges.caveats: Most mortality evidence here is population-level and observational or quasi-experimental rather than individually randomized, because national cash-transfer programs are rarely trialed in that way. Effects also appear to depend on transfer adequacy, coverage, and the surrounding public-health infrastructure, so the edge should not be read as equally strong in every setting.

evidence.citation: Cavalcanti DM et al 2025 Lancet Public Health
evidence.notes: Health effects of the Brazilian Conditional Cash Transfer programme over 20 years and projections to 2030: a retrospective analysis and modelling study.

evidence.citation: Owusu-Addo E et al 2014 Int J Public Health
evidence.notes: The impact of conditional cash transfers on child health in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review.

evidence.citation: Souza AA et al 2021 BMC Public Health
evidence.notes: Combination of conditional cash transfer program and environmental health interventions reduces child mortality: an ecological study of Brazilian municipalities.

new_entities.description: A population-level cash-transfer policy, often targeted to low-income households, intended to reduce poverty and improve health-related conditions.
